A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IGenBench study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. Visual inspection resolved extraction artifacts in the prompt figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten image-generation models, human-evaluator alignment, chart-type performance, data-leakage testing, and evaluator error analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original analyses of evaluator bias, reference-image similarity, prompt-length sensitivity, and question-type correlations.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, question augmentation, and binary verification remain unchanged. The sentence-by-sentence question generation newly explained in v2 Section 4.1 was already specified in v1 Appendix F, Figure 44, retained as v2 Figure 18.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 600 benchmark cases across 30 chart types and retain the 100 recent Visual Capitalist cases used for leakage testing. The new analyses reuse existing coverage. Reducing the displayed case gallery does not reduce the reported evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D.5 introduces a distinct family of scoring comparators: CLIP Image Similarity, SSIM, PSNR, and LPIPS, evaluated alongside Q-ACC in Tables 4–5. The ten generator models and the original MLLM evaluator candidates remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include evaluating a stratified 30-item sample with three evaluators, computing four reference-image similarity metrics, separating prompt tokens into data and semantic portions, and estimating question-type correlations within models. These substantially expand validation procedures while retaining the original main benchmark protocol.

E4.justification: v2 retains the chart-type, leakage, and evaluator-error analyses and adds four substantial investigations in D.4–D.7: provider bias, reference-similarity usefulness, prompt-length sensitivity, and question-type redundancy. Appendix E also contracts from 30 illustrated cases to four, with the proportional-area example retained in the main text.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly describes the existing 100 resamples as bootstrap samples; it does not establish increased repetition. D.7 adds within-model correlation estimation followed by averaging and identifies undefined correlations. The new caption's '25 questions' conflicts with the unchanged body's '25 examples,' leaving the resampling unit ambiguous.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained chart-type results are unchanged, including Nanobanana-Pro's 0.90 Q-ACC and 0.49 I-ACC. New Tables 3–7 report cross-evaluator ranking correlations of at least 0.95, CLIP–Q-ACC correlation of 0.30, prompt-length correlation of −0.573, and question-type correlations up to 0.21. Many individual case scores disappear with the shortened gallery.

T1.justification: The verification function, Q-ACC and I-ACC definitions, question-set construction, and sampling algorithm are unchanged. The added correlation analyses introduce empirical evidence rather than new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a dedicated infographic-generation benchmark, interpretable question-based evaluation, tiered model performance, data-fidelity bottlenecks, and difficulty achieving complete correctness.

C2.justification: D.4–D.7 add substantive interpretations concerning evaluator-provider robustness, the limitations of reference similarity, data volume as a source of difficulty, and question-type nonredundancy. Section 7 expands the stated exclusions from aesthetics to communicative effectiveness and accessibility, explaining their relationship to reliability.

D1.justification: The added analyses document sampling, prompt-token partitions, and correlation aggregation. Appendix E now directs readers to the project website for the complete case gallery previously embedded in the PDF. Existing construction settings, human instructions, and pipeline prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including ChartMark, PromptMagician, DeepEye, Vividoc, and AutoWebWorld. Related work expands the discussion of template and asset-library constraints in code-based generation, while retaining the paper's original benchmark positioning.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify prompt decomposition, related work, and limitations; update the appendix overview; and add corresponding-author information and acknowledgments. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with the substantial additions concentrated in new scientific analyses.

P2.justification: v2 adds five analytical tables and substantially reorganizes the appendix's visual content, retaining four of the former 30 case figures. It also expands captions, relocates Figures 3 and 6, and adjusts prompt-figure placement and sizing. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added cross-provider check and diagnostic analyses strengthen support for the evaluation framework, and the expanded limitations clarify its scope. However, D.5 reports 7,096 item-model pairs despite specifying 600 items and ten models, leaving its analysis population unexplained. Gallery condensation improves brevity but makes most case-level visual evidence external to the PDF. Together, these support a limited net improvement.
